The main takeaway from our work is that
the reverberation lag can be measured with high precision in a bright Seyfert galaxy with Kepler-like photometric sampling.

reverberation mapping is a viable technique even for active galactic nuclei with very high luminosities, as long as the light curve sampling is sufficiently dense and the source is observed over the full range of variability states.

Zw 229-15 is a promising candidate for reverberation-mapped black hole mass measurements, and that it will be possible to obtain high-quality black hole mass measurements in a number of other Kepler Seyfert galaxies.
